cases.scenario: GET /api/health returns status ok and tools count
cases.precondition: Server is running with MCP tool manager initialized
cases.expected_result: HTTP 200; JSON response {"status": "ok", "tools": <tools_count>} where tools_count is an integer ≥ 0

cases.scenario: GET /api/health returns tools count 0 when no tools registered
cases.precondition: Server is running but MCP tool manager has an empty _tools list
cases.expected_result: HTTP 200; JSON response {"status": "ok", "tools": 0}

cases.scenario: GET /api/health returns tools count equal to number of registered tools
cases.precondition: Server is running with exactly 5 tools registered in MCP tool manager
cases.expected_result: HTTP 200; JSON response {"status": "ok", "tools": 5}

cases.scenario: GET /api/health returns tools count when many tools registered
cases.precondition: Server is running with 1000 tools registered (large count)
cases.expected_result: HTTP 200; JSON response {"status": "ok", "tools": 1000}

cases.scenario: Calculator raises ValueError with meaningful message
cases.precondition: Server is running; the calculator function is instrumented to raise ValueError
cases.test_data: POST /api/calc with JSON body that causes a ValueError in the calculator

cases.expected_result: HTTP status 400; body is JSON {"error": "invalid inputs: ..."} where the message starts with 'invalid inputs:' and includes the error detail

cases.expected_result: HTTP status 400; body is JSON {"error": "invalid inputs: division by zero"}

cases.scenario: Send exactly 90 requests within 10 seconds from the same IP, then one more request
cases.precondition: Server is running; client IP is fixed (e.g., 127.0.0.1)
cases.test_data: 91 consecutive POST requests to any /api endpoint, each with a small body, sent as fast as possible
steps: Send 90 POST requests to any /api endpoint in rapid succession (within 10 seconds)
Send one more POST request immediately after
Receive the response for the 91st request
cases.expected_result: The 90th request returns success (200); the 91st request returns HTTP status 429; body is JSON {"error": "rate limit exceeded, slow down"}

cases.scenario: Send 91 requests within 10 seconds and verify the 91st is rate-limited
cases.precondition: Server is running; client IP is fixed (e.g., 127.0.0.1)
cases.test_data: 91 POST requests to any /api endpoint in quick succession
steps: Send 91 POST requests to any /api endpoint as quickly as possible
Record the response of the last (91st) request
cases.expected_result: The 91st request receives HTTP 429 and body {"error": "rate limit exceeded, slow down"}

cases.scenario: Send 90 requests then wait 11 seconds and send another request; rate limit should reset
cases.precondition: Server is running; client IP is fixed
cases.test_data: 90 requests followed by 11-second pause, then 1 more request
steps: Send 90 POST requests to any /api endpoint quickly
Send one more POST request to any /api endpoint
cases.expected_result: The 91st request (after waiting) should succeed with 200 status (not 429)

cases.scenario: Send 91 requests with different IP addresses and ensure only the exceeding client gets limited
cases.precondition: Server is running; two different client IPs are simulated
cases.test_data: From IP A: 91 requests; from IP B: 1 request
steps: Simulate client IP A and send 91 requests quickly
Simulate client IP B and send 1 request
cases.expected_result: IP A's 91st request receives 429; IP B's single request receives 200

cases.scenario: Positive: all required security headers are present in a normal response
steps: Send GET request to /api/health using TestClient
cases.expected_result: Response status is 200 and headers contain every key from the predefined set: x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, strict-transport-security, cross-origin-opener-policy, content-security-policy.

cases.scenario: Negative (Boundary): response with no content (204) still receives all security headers
cases.precondition: Server is running, endpoint returns 204 (e.g., OPTIONS on /api/health)
steps: Send OPTIONS request to /api/health using TestClient
cases.expected_result: Response status is 204 (or equivalent) and all six security headers (x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, strict-transport-security, cross-origin-opener-policy, content-security-policy) are present in the response headers.

cases.scenario: Negative (Boundary): error response (400) still receives all security headers
steps: Send GET request to /api/nav?code=abc using TestClient
cases.expected_result: Response status is 400 and all six security headers (x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, strict-transport-security, cross-origin-opener-policy, content-security-policy) are present in the response headers.

cases.scenario: Negative: response with null or missing body still includes all headers
steps: Send GET request to a non-existent route using TestClient
cases.expected_result: Response status is 404 and all six security headers (x-content-type-options, referrer-policy, permissions-policy, strict-transport-security, cross-origin-opener-policy, content-security-policy) are present in the response headers.
